title: Electronic Toroidal Metals: Landau Theory and Magnetoelectric Fingerprints
abstract: Toroidal order is a higher-rank multipolar order whose intrinsic realization in itinerant-electron systems remains unexplored. Here, we develop a generic theory of the electronic toroidal metal (ETM), in which toroidal order emerges spontaneously from electronic degrees of freedom near the Fermi surfaces. Because candidate toroidal bilinears can overlap by symmetry with the uniform charge current, we formulate a projected instability criterion that removes the noncondensable current component. Within this current-orthogonal sector, we identify a soft collective mode in the $\mathcal{P}$-odd and $\mathcal{T}$-odd particle-hole channel and demonstrate that ETM arises as a Fermi-liquid instability. We then define the toroidal moment in an itinerant system through the antisymmetric magnetoelectric response tensor. We further establish an intimate connection between this response and the topology of pseudospin texture: the rearrangement of pseudospin vortices changes the winding structure of the Fermi surfaces and markedly enhances the magnetoelectric response. ETM also exhibits characteristic nonlinear charge transport, including a pronounced enhancement of its interband quantum-geometric contribution. Our results establish ETM as a distinct metallic Landau phase and provide a general framework for understanding toroidal order generated by itinerant electrons.
summary: This work develops a general Landau theory for Electronic Toroidal Metals (ETM), showing how toroidal order can spontaneously arise in itinerant electron systems. The theory uses advanced projection techniques to isolate the physical instability, predicting unique signatures in the magnetoelectric response and nonlinear charge transport. It establishes ETM as a distinct metallic phase governed by Fermi-liquid instabilities.
main_problem: To develop a generic theory for the electronic toroidal metal (ETM), where toroidal order spontaneously emerges from electronic degrees of freedom near the Fermi surfaces in itinerant-electron systems.
main_result: ETM is established as a distinct metallic Landau phase, characterized by a soft collective mode and a unique enhancement of nonlinear charge transport linked to pseudospin texture topology.
method: The theory employs a projected instability criterion (Schur projection) to handle the overlap between toroidal candidates and the uniform charge current, leading to a Fermi-liquid instability analysis.
model_or_system: The study focuses on itinerant electron systems, using a minimal two-band Hamiltonian on a square lattice as a prototype for spin-orbit-coupled systems.
key_observables: Antisymmetric magnetoelectric response tensor, nonlinear charge transport ($\sigma_{interQMD}$), and the continuous evolution of the toroidal moment ($T$).
important_parameters: The instability is governed by the soft mode appearing in the P-odd and T-odd particle-hole channel.
main_assumptions: The primary technical hurdle addressed is the overlap of toroidal candidates with the uniform charge current, necessitating the Schur projection to select the physical instability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of various nonlinear conductivity contributions (NLD, interQMD, intraQMD) and show the momentum-space distribution of the interband quantum metric near pseudospin vortices.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first formulating the instability criterion, then using a Schur projection formalism on a minimal model to derive the effective mean-field Hamiltonian, and finally analyzing the resulting nonlinear transport signatures.
why_interesting: The concept of a higher-rank multipolar order (toroidal) emerging from itinerant electrons provides a rich theoretical framework for understanding exotic metallic phases beyond standard charge or spin ordering.
